title: Alcaraz Completes a Historic Comeback With ATP Finals Triumph
summary:
Carlos Alcaraz ended the men's tennis season the way he started it: holding a trophy and smiling. In January, the 23-year-old Spaniard won the Australian Open and completed the career Grand Slam, winning all four of the sport's biggest tournaments. Ten months later, he stood as the winner in Turin, lifting his first ATP Finals title after beating world number one Alexander Zverev on Sunday.

It was a remarkable finish to a strange year. For four months, Alcaraz barely picked up a racquet. A wrist injury kept him out of most of the clay season and all of the grass-court season. His comeback began 84 days ago at the US Open, where his lack of match fitness showed, and he lost a five-set quarter-final against Ben Shelton.

Since then, he has been almost unstoppable. Alcaraz has won 21 of his 22 matches, including each of the past 14, and taken titles at four of the five tournaments he has played. This was his third straight tournament win, after the Vienna Open and the Paris Masters earlier in November, and he has won his past nine matches against fellow top-10 players. Along the way, he became the youngest man to win all four Grand Slams and the season-ending Finals.

Even a heavily strapped left leg could not stop him in Turin, after he injured his hamstring on Wednesday. Zverev had a strong year too, rising to the top of the rankings for the first time after winning his first two major titles and recording a tour-leading 69 match wins. Alcaraz, already a seven-time Slam winner and a former world number one, is now ranked third, behind Zverev and Jannik Sinner.

'The injury made me realise what's really important,' Alcaraz said. 'It's not winning. It's just about playing tennis.'
why_it_matters: Alcaraz's comeback shows how athletes recover from long injuries and why enjoying the sport can matter as much as winning. His story also shows how quickly rankings can change at the top of men's tennis.

background_read: The ATP Finals is the tennis season's closing event, where the year's best players compete for one last title.
A Grand Slam is one of the four biggest tournaments in tennis, and winning all four over a career is one of the sport's greatest achievements.
Players are ranked by their results, and the world number one is the top-ranked player.
Alcaraz's year shows how an injury can keep a player out of the game for months, and how hard the road back can be.
